name: Virgo
introduction: is the Virgin, often identified with the goddess of justice or harvest. It is the second-largest constellation and the largest of the zodiac, best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Around 130 BC, Hipparchus compared his measurements of [Spica](hip:65474) with older records and discovered the slow precession of Earth’s axis.

Beyond Virgo’s stars lies the Virgo Cluster, about 50 million light-years away, with more than a thousand galaxies. At its heart, the giant galaxy M87 hosts a supermassive black hole whose shadow was imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Spica](hip:65474), a hot blue-white star 250 light-years away, is a close binary whose stars are distorted into egg shapes by their mutual gravity.

[Porrima](hip:61941) is a binary of two nearly identical stars, and [Vindemiatrix](hip:63608), “the grape-gatherer”, rose with the Sun at grape-harvest time in ancient times. [Heze](hip:66249) and [Minelauva](hip:63090) complete the figure.
Nearby in space, the red dwarf [Ross 128](id:ross-128), 11 light-years away, has a temperate Earth-sized planet, and [61 Virginis](id:cns5-3273) is a Sun-like star with planets.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Virgo also contains the Sombrero Galaxy, M104, with its dark dust lane, and 3C 273, the first quasar identified and the brightest in the sky.
